added_failures_note: The reviewed run declares no baseline_suite or after_suite arm (classification.json records after_suite: null) because it adds no test file; its gate is the instrument's own control and capture pair, whose gate.log reads CONTROL-RESULT PASS, CAPTURE-RESULT PASS and EXIT=0, so there are no failures to subtract.

findings.text: The controls table quotes 'live: REFINED_FROM edges 1,771', but the committed capture this record rests on (scc-chaincap-remeasure.json, revision c9bb3c280) records refined_from_edges 1,770 and gate.log prints 1770; the drift paragraph covers only the cut's population and published totals, so a reader comparing the fragment with its own capture meets two unexplained values for a control count.

The summary states the census was 're-read on the live graph at commit fc99c61f0', but the instrument did not exist at fc99c61f - it was untracked working-tree content there - and the committed capture records revision c9bb3c280, so the record names a revision at which its own measure cannot be reproduced.

The publish-boundary assertion tests only that chain_cap_at_publish_boundary is non-empty. The fixture plants ctrl_chaincap_childless precisely to sit in the export population but not the published set, yet nothing asserts the boundary equals {'ctrl_chaincap_unsourced_parent'}, so a regression that intersected the no-ancestor cohort with the population instead of the published set would still pass the control.

capture prints 'CONNECTED uri=unknown' because it reads gc._uri, an attribute GraphClient does not expose, so the capture log records no endpoint and the live-graph provenance of the headline numbers rests on the numbers alone; resolving and printing the connected URI would make the log show what it read.

The declared figure path docs/figures/sn-catalog-consistency/scc-chaincap-remeasure was never written, so the ancestry split and the publish boundary are presented only as tables where the repository's figure convention asks for a graphic that would carry the same comparison.
